title: Shipped my puzzle game today, built mostly in conversation with Claude. The most useful thing the AI built wasn't the game, it was a bot that played it
author: Hidden-Method
selftext:
Cantrip went live on Google Play this morning. It's a falling-block puzzle where you rotate the piece as usual, and you can also swipe to turn the whole playfield 90°, FEZ-style. Same blocks, new front.



In real life I'm an engineer, not a game developer. Most of the game was built in a long back-and-forth with Claude: one HTML/JS file that grew into the full game, later wrapped in an Android WebView with Play Billing. A few things from that process that I think are worth talking about:



The best decision was building a headless simulator before tuning anything. A bot plays the game on its own, thousands of runs. It told me two uncomfortable things. First, my score targets, a neat quadratic curve on paper, became unreachable above level 15. Second, the flip, the whole point of the game, was structurally optional: a decent player could ignore it entirely. I rebuilt the targets from measured scoring rates instead of theory, and decided to keep the flip optional but make it pay off, rather than force it.



The bot also killed an assumption about Endless Mode. I expected more garbage rows to make runs shorter. They made them longer, because each garbage row has a single gap. Find it and you get an almost free line. Runs came out as "three minutes or forever". The honest limit: the bot has unlimited thinking time and zero reaction time, so at the hard end its numbers only mean "the board stays solvable", not "humans survive".



Where it went wrong: the AI is confidently wrong exactly where you don't check. An early draft of my store text claimed you can't rotate the piece in my game. You can. The first version of the billing code was missing a token that current Play Billing versions expect, and that only got caught in a separate review pass. My takeaway: treat it like a very fast colleague whose work you review, not like an oracle.



Question for you: when you balance with AI, do you trust simulated players, or only real playtests? Where did a simulation lie to you?



Free, no ads, one optional unlock: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.hiddenmethod.cantrip](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.hiddenmethod.cantrip)

comments.author: qing-turn
comments.body: Same lesson here, and congrats on shipping! Our tower defense has a bot that plays full 30-wave runs headlessly, and the first thing it told us was that our difficulty targets were way off from what we assumed. It also became our regression test: if a change makes the "average player" bot lose earlier, we find out before the build goes out. Did you tune your bot to play like a human, or just optimally?
